The *Mātuposakagijjhajātaka* (Ja 399) is a birth story situated in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. According to the traditional narrative setting, the Buddha recounted the tale while residing at Jetavana concerning a monk who supported his mother, opening with the verse line "How will the old folks" [SuttaCentral].

Textual reuse analysis by DharmaNexus documents extensive internal reuse between the Jātaka verses and the commentary, showing 12 shared passages (totaling 1,125 characters) with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Tatiyo bhāgo), including a substantial correspondence across segments §2.1–7.4 [DharmaNexus]. Four modern translations in four languages are indexed on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
